value.title: Claude Code direct delivery over the messaging socket
value.summary: Deliver to Claude Code seats over Claude's own messaging socket with Held actually observable, concurrency refused rather than resolved, and one row per seat.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: req-0002. The shipped Rust UDS transport cannot observe Held for two independent reasons (an unroutable reply address, and a status matcher keyed to a wire shape the CLI never emits), so a message parked behind a human's approval dialog is reported Delivered. Status frames carry no correlation id anywhere in their lifecycle, which forces positional correlation and therefore one message in flight per connection. Separately, registration adopts a pre-bind row by seat id alone, so a daemon-spawned seat strands a phantom row and loses the rpc_port stamped on it. Two units fix these; the evidence base is first-party and measured (scratch/woodpecker-poc/FINDINGS.md).

sections.name: goals
value: Held and Denied are observable on the live wire, not inferred from silence.
A timeout is never upgraded to Delivered — the honest-receipt vocabulary holds.
Concurrency is refused at the transport, never guessed at.
One seat, one row, with the stamped rpc_port surviving onto the row consumers read.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Improving the tmux send-keys path; it is being replaced, not repaired.
Flipping the crossSessionInbound consent default — that is Jordan's ruling, not this plan's.
Verb parity, and anything on the prime-governance branch.

value.claim: Held is observable end to end against a live Claude CLI, proven by a test witnessed RED on the pre-fix tree.
value.receipt: crates/transport/tests/live_held_observation.rs::an_unmarked_message_is_observed_held_on_the_live_wire. WITNESSED RED at 5f41cda5 (Delivered{InjectedToTransport}, 153.9ms, FAILED) before any transport change; GREEN at 0be4bc19 (Held, 62.9-73.6ms). Re-run: PIJ_LIVE_CLAUDE_PID=<non-accepting pid> cargo test -p pij-transport --test live_held_observation -- --ignored.

value.claim: Reverting from= to the unroutable literal makes the hold receipt vanish, and reverting the status matcher to the bare type makes Held unreachable — each mutation fails its own guard.
value.receipt: Mutations re-executed independently by the reviewer, counts matching mine: M1 from= -> "uds:pij-daemon" = 4 FAILED; M2 classify_status bare type only = 5 FAILED; M3 worker Held -> release_body = 2 FAILED; M4 drop proc.is_none() = 1 FAILED (bound-row arm); M5 drop pane = 1 FAILED; M7 disable the adoption fallback = 1 FAILED. Plus, post-review: shared reply address = 1 FAILED (concurrent_deliveries), M6 = 1 FAILED (port-inheritance arm). NOT COUNTED: the_control_shape_is_what_the_live_cli_actually_emits stays GREEN under M2 — it pins the fixture, it does not guard the decoder.

value.claim: Two messages in flight on one connection are REFUSED, not correlated by guesswork.
value.receipt: crates/transport/src/uds.rs::exactly_one_message_is_ever_in_flight_on_one_connection asserts the WIRE (auth + exactly ONE frame, from= routable and in the recipient's namespace), and concurrent_deliveries_do_not_share_a_reply_address drives TWO REAL deliveries and fails when the reply path is mutated to a single shared address. Concurrency is refused by construction: a private reply address per delivery.

value.claim: A registration that BINDS A FRESHLY SPAWNED INCARNATION adopts its pre-bind row: matched on spawn_id AND pane AND the row being unbound, leaving one row on the pane with its stamped rpc_port_intent preserved.
value.receipt: crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs::spawned_registration_adopts_prebind_row_and_preserves_port, built from the FakeTmux launch argv and list_panes, never the spawn response. Pre-fix red re-derived by the reviewer (M7). Adoption requires spawn_id AND pane AND the row being unbound: registration_cannot_adopt_a_spawn_match_that_is_already_bound fails under M4.

value.claim: THE DISCRIMINATING ARM: a registration NOT preceded by a fresh allocation — an ordinary re-registration of an existing seat — does NOT adopt and does NOT inherit an rpc_port it was never stamped. A spawn_id+pane match against an ALREADY BOUND row must not adopt it either.
value.receipt: crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs::reregistration_prefers_exact_id_over_spawn_match_without_fresh_allocation, registration_cannot_adopt_a_spawn_match_from_another_pane (M5), and registration_does_not_inherit_a_port_stamped_for_another_incarnation — the last added after the reviewer showed the port-inheritance half was VACUOUS (its M6 left the whole daemon http suite green because the row's port was already None). M6 now fails exactly that test.

value.claim: Live round trip on the real fleet, both arms, three observers: bypass-marked delivered with no dialog and byte-exact above 1022 bytes against an --accept-inbound seat; unmarked message observed Held before any human click against a non-accepting seat.
value.receipt: ALL THREE ARMS LIVE on the composed head: Held 62.9ms (non-accepting seat); Delivered 3000B/40 contiguous lines into an --accept-inbound seat, real type=user turn, no hold record; Refused 2.24s through the SHIPPED transport, operator's Deny recorded as an INPUT. SCOPE QUALIFIER (reviewer F3): the held and refused arms stamp cross_session_inbound_accept=Some(true) on a NON-accepting seat, which is the stamp/reality drift that is the only production trigger for these outcomes today — the arms are honest about the transport and do not demonstrate a configuration the fleet currently has.

value.claim: Full gate green on the composed, rebased tree, unfiltered, with cargo's own exit code, then cross-model review.
value.receipt: pij-gate at 0be4bc19: toolchain PASS (rustc 1.98.0 == pin), lock, fmt, clippy, test, arch — exit code 0, run as `~/.cargo/bin/cargo run -p pij-testkit --bin pij-gate` because a bare cargo here is homebrew 1.95 and ignores the pin silently. Independently re-run by the reviewer and by the o-prime on this head. Cross-model review (GLM 5.3 Flash) complete: five findings fixed, four escalated as oq-1104..1107.

value.title: u-uds — honest UDS transport
value.brief: Bind a reply listener in the recipient's socket namespace and advertise a routable from=; accept the real status shape; refuse concurrency. Observation test FIRST, witnessed red.
value.objective: Make Held and Denied observable and honest without regressing the receipt vocabulary.
delivers: Routable reply address so the CLI can deliver peer_message_status
Status decoder keyed to type==control / action==peer_message_status
One message in flight per connection, refused rather than resolved
Fixtures replaced with captured wire lines rather than invented ones

value.title: u-adopt — registration adopts the spawned identity
value.brief: Adopt the pre-bind row on spawn_id (+pane) when the id lookup misses, and stop clearing the rpc_port_intent that the same registration stamped.
value.objective: One seat, one row, port surviving onto the row consumers read.
delivers: spawn_id-keyed adoption fallback in the register route
rpc_port_intent preserved on the binding registration
Witness built from the launched environment

value.title: Compose and prove
value.brief: Merge u-adopt first, then u-uds; re-run the full gate on the composed rebased tree; live round trip on both recipient configurations; cross-model review before the PR.
value.objective: Prove the fix and the declared head agree.
delivers: Composed rebased head with an unfiltered gate transcript
Live two-arm integration proof with three observers
Cross-model review that re-derives the arms by execution

sections.name: risks_assumptions
sections.value: r1 A third independent reason Held stays unreachable — retired by making the FIRST commit a live observation test, before any refactor. r2 Building on the fork's spec where it diverges from the installed build — retired by verifying each borrowed claim against Claude CLI 2.1.251; four of six of that spec's Copilot claims diverged when tested, and its status-frame shape is already known wrong. r3 Silently resolving concurrency instead of refusing it — retired by the two-in-flight mutation. r4 An acceptance test written against the spawn response rather than the launched environment — retired by the discriminating arm that re-registers with no fresh allocation. r5 Regressing toward the fork's `acked` — retired by a test that silence is never upgraded past InjectedToTransport. ASSUMPTION, measured not assumed: a reply listener bound inside the recipient's socket namespace is accepted as a routable reply address; verified live 2026-08-31, held receipt returned in 72ms.

value.question: Should crossSessionInbound=accept default ON for daemon-spawned Claude seats? It is implemented and opt-in, defaults false, so the UDS transport is off for every seat on the fleet today.
value.note: Consent is an act, not a default flipped on the operator's behalf. Neither arm is being built until this is ruled. COUPLED (o-prime): the consent default may not flip ON before the held-delivery backoff lands, because Held's only consumer was an immediate retry — a dialog storm at the operator — dormant only while the transport is off. Both halves ship together or not at all. The backoff has now landed.

value.question: RESOLVED — NOT A DEFECT. Originally filed as 'Claude writes socket and key before the session record, so discovery has a startup window'. That generalised ONE abnormal seat into a timing law and was wrong.
value.note: Four controlled runs 2026-08-31. (A) cwd = an already-trusted worktree, --dangerously-skip-permissions: record, key and socket ALL present within 5s — no startup window exists. (B) cwd /tmp, no bypass flag and (C) cwd /tmp, WITH bypass flag: key and socket present, record ABSENT — both sitting on the FOLDER-TRUST prompt, captured verbatim from the pane. Bypass-permissions does not skip folder trust. The true fact: a session PARKED AT THE PRE-SESSION TRUST GATE publishes a live authenticable socket and has not written a session record. So discovery must NOT be changed: treating socket+key as proof would deliver into a process that has not started a session and may never, because it is waiting on a human at a modal. The record's absence is the honest not-ready signal and is already doing its job. o-prime's earlier ruling to move the fix into discovery is WITHDRAWN. Instrument failures behind the original error, recorded because they will bite someone else: a blank tmux capture read as 'still booting' when the pane was on a modal, and `pgrep -P <pane_pid>` returning an MCP child instead of the claude process. FUTURE DIAGNOSTIC, not built: socket present + record absent for >N seconds = a human is blocked at a modal on that seat, which is invisible to pij while looking spawn-successful.

value.question: Can a sparse status stream (not all messages held) ever be aligned by an observable not yet found?
value.note: Disclosed unprobed in req-0002. The one-in-flight conclusion does not depend on closing it.

value.question: Held and Refused are DRIFT-ONLY reachable today: every live Claude session record carries crossSessionInbound=null, can_deliver refuses before any write, and an accepting seat never holds. Should the PR say so, and should the descriptor consume the CLI record's own consent flag?
value.note: Reviewer F3 + mirror gap, verified live: zero accepting seats on the fleet. A hand-started seat whose operator DID launch with accept is never served, because the register path never reads the consent flag that is sitting on disk. Adjacent to oq-1101. O-PRIME: stays open COUPLED to oq-1101 — one consent decision with three dependents now: the default, the held backoff, and this mirror gap.

value.question: The direct send path claims note_delivered(InjectedToTransport) BEFORE transport.deliver and compensates only Queued/Err, so a Held or Refused leaves the ledger saying DELIVERED for a message that was denied. Intended, or store the outcome with the claim?
value.note: Reviewer F6. Both directions prevent the worse outcome, but the ledger and the receipt stream disagree and an auditor sees delivered for a refused message. O-PRIME RULING: follow-up, NOT in-branch, and NOT the naive fix — compensating note_delivered on Refused would make a refused message look re-deliverable and re-prompt the human. The honest fix is a TERMINAL WORD IN THE LEDGER VOCABULARY, the same add-the-word lesson one layer down.

value.question: A human slower than HOLD_GRACE still yields Held; the job then backs off and re-delivers, re-prompting someone who may have already denied, and the park reason says 'has not approved' rather than 'answered no'. Fix direction: keep the reply inbox alive across the job lifecycle and let the worker cancel the retry on a denial.
value.note: Reviewer addendum. This is a transport->worker contract change, so it is a seam change and not patched in this branch. O-PRIME RULING: direction approved, follow-up coupled to consent-ON. Include the park-reason wording: it says 'the recipient has not approved it' when the truth may be 'answered no' — a report must not misname its state.

value.question: PRE-EXISTING, and plan 110's tests now enshrine it: a bound row re-registering has rpc_port_intent CLEARED, while the allocator treats live rows' intents as the RESERVED set — so spawn(port) -> register -> re-register frees a port a live Copilot is listening on.
value.note: Reviewer, found while re-deriving. Not introduced here, but it contradicts the u-adopt goal 'the stamped rpc_port surviving onto the row consumers read', which holds only until the seat's next registration. O-PRIME: minting PRD req-0008 'registration idempotence' — a re-register must never destroy live state (port intents, consent stamps). The tests in this branch that enshrine the current behaviour are named there, so whoever fixes it knows which greens to expect to flip.
